chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Humran ibn Ayn, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'May I be sacrificed for you! We pray with these people on Friday, and they pray at the time (different to ours). So what should we do?' He said: 'Pray with them.'

So Humran went out to Zurara and said to him: 'We have been ordered to pray with them in their prayer.' Zurara said: 'This cannot be except with explanation (ta'wil).' Humran said to him: 'Rise until you hear from him.'

He said: 'So we entered upon him, and Zurara said to him: May I be sacrificed for you! Humran claims that you ordered us to pray with them, but I denied that.' He said to us: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to pray two rak'at with them. So when they finished, he would stand and add two rak'at to them.'

key_terms.أَهْلُ الصَّلَاةِ: The people of prayer (referring to the congregation)

ai.seo_question: How should Shia Muslims pray behind non-Shia Muslims during Friday prayers?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes the permissibility of praying behind non-Shia Muslims during Friday prayers, a ruling grounded in 'ta'wil' (interpretive flexibility) rather than strict conformity to their prayer structure. It highlights the precedent set by Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin), who prayed two rak'at with the congregation and then added two more, illustrating a practical method of validating the communal prayer while maintaining distinct Shia jurisprudential integrity. This approach underscores the Shia principle of avoiding unnecessary division in communal worship when the core validity is preserved.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Hadeed, from Jameel Bin Darraj, from Humran Bin Ayn who said,

‘I said to Abu Ja’farasws, ‘May I be sacrificed for youasws! We tend to pray the Salāt with them (general Muslims) on the day of Friday, and they are praying in the time (different to ours). So what should we do?’ So heasws said: ‘Pray Salāt with them’.

So Humran went out to Zurara and said to him, ‘Heasws has ordered us that we should pray with them in their Salāts’. So Zurara said, ‘This cannot happen to be except with the explanation’. So Humran said to him, ‘Arise until you hear from himasws’.

He said, ‘So we went over to himasws and Zurara said to himasws, ‘May I be sacrificed for youasws! Humran claims that youasws ordered us that we should be praying Salāt with them (general Muslims), but I denied that’. So heasws said to us: ‘Aliasws Bin Al-Husaynasws used to pray two Rak’at of Salāt with them. So when they were free, heasws would stand and increase two Rak’at upon these’.
en.sarwar: 7. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Hadid from Jamil ibn Darraj from Humran ibn ’A‘yan who has said the following:

“I once said to Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, we perform Salah (prayer) with these people on Friday and they perform in a certain time. What must we do? He (the Imam) said, ‘Perform Salah (prayer) with them?

Humran then went to Zurarah and said to him, ‘We are commanded to perform Salah (prayer) with them with their Salah (prayer)? Zurarah said, ‘This cannot be accepted without interpretation? Humran said to him, ‘Come and hear it from him (the Imam)?

He (the narrator) has said that both went to him (the Imam) and Zurarah said, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, Humran thinks you have commanded us to perform Salah (prayer) with them and I did not accept it? He (the Imam) said to us, ‘Ali ibn al- Husayn, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, would say two Rak‘at with them and when they would complete he stand up to perform two more Rak‘at?” (Ahadith 1-7 are best explained by fatwa.)
